metadata.description: Hardware connectors, cables, electrical specifications, and usage.

data.name: USB Type-C
data.purpose: General-purpose data, display, and power connection
data.voltage: 5V nominal, USB Power Delivery up to 48V
data.power_delivery: Up to 240W with USB Power Delivery
notes: The connector shape does not by itself determine supported speed.

data.name: USB Type-A
data.power_delivery: Typically up to 7.5W under common USB standards
notes: USB Type-A remains common on desktop systems.

data.name: USB Type-B
notes: Type-B is mainly used on peripheral devices.

data.name: USB Mini-B
notes: Largely replaced by Micro-B and USB Type-C.

data.name: USB Micro-B
notes: Commonly replaced by USB Type-C.

data.name: USB 3 Micro-B
notes: The connector is physically wider than Micro-B USB 2.0.

data.name: USB Micro-AB
data.purpose: USB On-The-Go host and peripheral connection
notes: Supports both Micro-A and Micro-B plugs.

data.name: USB4
data.purpose: High-bandwidth USB data and protocol tunneling
data.power_delivery: Up to 240W through USB Power Delivery
notes: USB4 can tunnel multiple protocols through one connection.

data.name: Thunderbolt 3
data.purpose: High-speed data, display, and peripheral connection
notes: Thunderbolt 3 uses the USB Type-C connector.

data.name: Thunderbolt 4
data.purpose: High-speed data, display, and docking connection
notes: Thunderbolt 4 tightened minimum capability requirements compared with Thunderbolt 3.

data.name: Thunderbolt 5
data.purpose: Very high-speed data and display connection
notes: Thunderbolt 5 supports higher bandwidth than Thunderbolt 4.

data.name: DisplayPort
data.bandwidth: Up to 80Gbps raw link rate with UHBR20
notes: DisplayPort supports adaptive sync and multi-display features.

data.name: Mini DisplayPort
data.purpose: Compact digital video and audio connection
notes: The same connector was used by Thunderbolt 1 and 2.

data.name: HDMI Type-A
notes: HDMI carries both digital audio and video.

data.name: Mini HDMI
data.purpose: Compact digital video and audio transmission
notes: Mini HDMI uses fewer physical dimensions than Type-A while keeping the same pin count.

data.name: Micro HDMI
data.purpose: Very compact digital video and audio transmission
notes: Micro HDMI is smaller than Mini HDMI.

data.name: DVI-D
notes: DVI-D carries digital video only.

data.name: DVI-I
notes: DVI-I includes pins for analog video.

data.name: VGA
notes: VGA is analog and has largely been replaced by digital interfaces.

data.name: SATA Data
notes: SATA III is commonly called SATA 6Gbps.

data.name: SATA Power
data.purpose: Power delivery to SATA storage devices
notes: Provides multiple DC voltage rails.

data.name: M.2 Key M
data.purpose: Direct motherboard connection for NVMe storage
data.power_delivery: Typically up to about 8W class device power
notes: Key M is the most common high-speed NVMe keying.

data.name: M.2 Key B
data.bandwidth: Up to PCIe x2 depending on implementation
notes: Key B supports fewer PCIe lanes than Key M.

data.name: M.2 Key B+M
data.bandwidth: Up to PCIe x2 depending on implementation
notes: B+M indicates two possible key notches.

data.name: M.2 Key E
data.bandwidth: PCIe x1 or USB depending on implementation
notes: Key E is widely used for motherboard Wi-Fi modules.

data.name: M.2 Key A
data.bandwidth: PCIe x1 or USB depending on implementation
notes: Key A is less common in modern desktop systems than Key E.

data.name: PCI Express x1
notes: Physical x1 slots can sometimes accept shorter or compatible devices of other sizes.

data.name: PCI Express x4
notes: Some x4 slots are physically open-ended.

data.name: PCI Express x8
notes: Common on workstations and servers.

data.name: PCI Express x16
notes: The x16 slot is the standard graphics card slot on desktop PCs.

data.name: PCI
notes: PCI has been replaced by PCI Express in modern PCs.

data.name: PCI-X
notes: PCI-X predates PCI Express.

data.name: DDR5 DIMM
notes: DDR5 DIMM keying prevents installation in DDR4 slots.

data.name: DDR4 DIMM
notes: DDR4 modules are not electrically compatible with DDR5 slots.

data.name: DDR3 DIMM
notes: DDR3 is no longer common on new desktop systems.

data.name: DDR5 SO-DIMM
notes: SO-DIMM modules are smaller than desktop DIMMs.

data.name: DDR4 SO-DIMM
notes: DDR4 SO-DIMM and DDR5 SO-DIMM use different electrical interfaces.

data.name: CAMM2
notes: CAMM2 is designed as a successor to conventional SO-DIMM designs in some systems.

data.name: 24-Pin ATX
notes: The 24-pin connector evolved from the older 20-pin ATX connector.

data.name: 20-Pin ATX
notes: Superseded by the 24-pin ATX connector.

data.name: 4-Pin ATX12V
notes: This connector is commonly called the 4-pin CPU power connector.

data.name: 8-Pin EPS12V
notes: Many modern motherboards provide one or more EPS connectors.

data.name: 6-Pin PCIe Power
notes: The connector supplements power supplied through the PCIe slot.

data.name: 8-Pin PCIe Power
notes: Often implemented as a 6+2 pin connector on power supplies.

data.name: 12VHPWR
notes: The connector carries both power and sideband sensing signals.

data.name: 12V-2x6
notes: 12V-2x6 is the updated connector design associated with the 12VHPWR family.

data.name: ATX12VO 10-Pin
data.power_delivery: Up to roughly 216-288W depending on current rating
notes: ATX12VO moves voltage conversion onto the motherboard.

data.name: Molex 4-Pin Peripheral
notes: Often called a Molex connector in PC building.

data.name: Berg Floppy Power
notes: Almost completely obsolete in modern PCs.

data.name: RJ45 Ethernet
data.power_delivery: PoE up to standard-dependent power levels
data.bandwidth: Up to 100Gbps depending on Ethernet standard
notes: RJ45 is commonly used as a name for the 8P8C connector used by Ethernet.

data.name: SFP
notes: SFP is commonly associated with Gigabit networking.

data.name: SFP+
notes: SFP+ is the 10Gbps evolution of SFP.

data.name: SFP28
notes: SFP28 uses the same general form factor as SFP and SFP+.

data.name: QSFP+
notes: QSFP+ combines four high-speed lanes.

data.name: QSFP28
notes: QSFP28 is commonly used for 100GbE.

data.name: 3.5mm TRS
notes: TRS provides tip, ring, and sleeve contacts.

data.name: 3.5mm TRRS
notes: Pin assignments can differ between CTIA and OMTP.

data.name: 6.35mm TRS
notes: Also called a quarter-inch connector.

data.name: RCA
data.purpose: Analog audio or composite video connection
notes: RCA is a connector family rather than a single digital standard.

data.name: TOSLINK
data.bandwidth: Typically up to 24-bit/192kHz PCM depending on device
notes: TOSLINK uses light instead of electrical signaling.

data.name: S/PDIF Coaxial
notes: S/PDIF can be carried over coaxial or optical connectors.

data.name: PS/2
notes: Some modern motherboards still include a combined PS/2 port.

data.name: RS-232 DB-9
notes: Often called a DB-9 even though DE-9 is the precise designation.

data.name: DB-25 Parallel
notes: Parallel ports are largely obsolete on consumer PCs.

data.name: Game Port
notes: The PC game port is obsolete.

data.name: FireWire 400
notes: FireWire is largely obsolete.

data.name: FireWire 800
notes: FireWire 800 doubled the nominal speed of FireWire 400.

data.name: U.2
notes: U.2 is also known as SFF-8639.

data.name: U.3
notes: U.3 is designed to support multiple storage protocols.

data.name: SAS SFF-8482
notes: SAS is designed for enterprise storage environments.

data.name: SlimSAS 4i
notes: SlimSAS reduces cable and connector size for dense systems.

data.name: SlimSAS 8i
notes: 8i carries twice the lane count of 4i.

data.name: OCuLink SFF-8611
data.purpose: Compact external or internal PCIe connection
notes: OCuLink is designed for PCIe signaling over compact cabling.

data.name: OCuLink SFF-8612
notes: SFF-8612 is a smaller OCuLink connector variant.

data.name: Front Panel Header
data.purpose: Connects case buttons and status LEDs
notes: Pin layouts vary by motherboard.

data.name: USB 2.0 Internal Header
data.power_delivery: Up to 500mA per standard USB 2.0 port
notes: Often called a 9-pin USB header.

data.name: USB 3 Internal Header
notes: Commonly used for front-panel USB 3 Type-A ports.

data.name: USB 3.2 Gen 2x2 Internal Header
notes: Designed for internal front-panel USB Type-C ports.

data.name: HD Audio Header
notes: Replaced older AC'97 front-panel audio headers on modern PCs.

data.name: TPM Header
data.purpose: Connects a discrete trusted platform module
notes: Many modern systems use firmware TPM instead of a physical header.

data.name: Fan Header
notes: Four-pin headers can control fan speed using PWM.

data.name: ARGB Header
notes: 5V ARGB must not be connected to a 12V RGB header.

data.name: 12V RGB Header
notes: 12V RGB and 5V ARGB are electrically different.

data.name: EPS CPU 4+4
notes: 4+4 allows the cable to fit boards requiring either 4 or 8 CPU power pins.

data.name: PCIe 6+2
notes: The detachable 2-pin section allows compatibility with both 6-pin and 8-pin GPU sockets.

data.name: RJ11
notes: RJ11 is smaller than the 8-position connector commonly used for Ethernet.

data.name: BNC
notes: BNC is widely used in test and professional video equipment.

data.name: SMA
notes: Desktop Wi-Fi motherboard antennas often use RP-SMA connectors.

data.name: RP-SMA
notes: RP-SMA is common on consumer Wi-Fi hardware.

data.name: Molex Micro-Fit 3.0
notes: Micro-Fit is designed for higher density than traditional Mini-Fit connectors.

data.name: Molex Mini-Fit Jr.
notes: Mini-Fit Jr. contacts are used in several common PC power connectors.

data.name: Micro-DVI
data.purpose: Compact digital and analog video connection
notes: Micro-DVI was used on some older Apple portable computers.

data.name: Thunderbolt 1
notes: Thunderbolt 1 combines PCI Express and DisplayPort protocols.

data.name: Thunderbolt 2
notes: Thunderbolt 2 increased aggregate bandwidth to 20Gbps.

data.name: USB 2.0 Type-A
notes: USB 2.0 remains widely used for low-bandwidth peripherals.

data.name: USB 3.2 Type-A
notes: USB 3.x Type-A connectors can be backward compatible with USB 2.0.

data.name: HDMI Internal Header
data.purpose: Internal HDMI connection for specialized systems
notes: Internal HDMI connectors are less common than external HDMI ports.

data.name: eSATA
notes: eSATA largely lost popularity to USB 3.x and USB Type-C.

data.name: USB Type-C DisplayPort Alt Mode
notes: A USB Type-C port does not necessarily support DisplayPort Alt Mode.

data.name: USB Power Delivery
data.purpose: Negotiated power delivery over USB Type-C
data.power_delivery: Up to 240W with current USB PD specifications
notes: USB Power Delivery is a power protocol rather than a separate physical connector.
